title: Fed's Warsh strikes hawkish tone on inflation at Jackson Hole, yields jump
content:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish keynote at the Jackson Hole symposium on 28 August 2026, warning that underlying inflation trends have not meaningfully improved despite softer summer CPI and PCE readings. His remarks reopened the possibility of a rate hike rather than the September cut markets had priced in. The speech followed data showing core PCE inflation held at 3.3% year-on-year in July, with spending stalling — giving the Fed some near-term room but doing little to ease Warsh's concerns about entrenched price pressures.

Treasury yields jumped on the remarks, with the two-year yield rising more than 12bp to **4.36%** and the 10-year up to **4.73%**. The dollar index extended its rebound to **99.67**, having touched a three-month low a week earlier. Equities initially wobbled before closing higher as investors repriced the odds of a September move.

title: Nvidia's blockbuster earnings send Nasdaq, chip stocks surging
content:
Nvidia trounced Wall Street forecasts in its fiscal second-quarter results, released after the close on 26 August 2026, with revenue more than doubling year-on-year on relentless AI-chip demand. Management guided to roughly 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, well above the 44% analysts at LSEG had pencilled in, reassuring investors that AI infrastructure spending shows no sign of slowing.

Nvidia shares jumped **8.7%**, lifting the Nasdaq Composite **1.6%** to a fresh high and the S&P 500 **0.7%**. The rally spread across the semiconductor supply chain, with Broadcom up 4.5% and Intel up 4%, while chip stocks in Japan and South Korea also gained, underscoring the AI trade's continued grip on global equity sentiment.

title: US-Canada trade war escalates as 50% tariffs take hold
content:
Trade talks between Washington and Ottawa collapsed on 22 August 2026, triggering US tariffs of **50%** on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods spanning dairy, alcohol, appliances and building materials. Canada responded on 25 August with retaliatory tariffs on more than 700 US products, due to take effect on 8 September, with Prime Minister Mark Carney vowing to match the levies "dollar for dollar" and declaring Canada effectively at war with the US economically.

The Canadian dollar slipped as much as **0.7%** to around **C$1.385** per USD, the weakest performance among G10 currencies, though losses proved fairly contained. Toronto's S&P/TSX composite swung between gains and losses before closing little changed, while the Dow Jones rose modestly; investors read the muted reaction as a sign a near-term trade deal remains unlikely.
